1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. What the exam is. The five domains. Question types. How the objectives are worded. A repeatable way to answer. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains. Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: What the exam is
1.text: What the exam is. Comp T I A Security plus V eight (S Y zero eight oh one) tests the knowledge of a security administrator with about two years of hands-on experience. You must identify, interpret and support incident response, assess security posture and recommend solutions, manage modern environments (cloud, mobile, hybrid), work with governance, risk and compliance, and apply mitigations for threats and vulnerabilities.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. Exam code. S Y zero eight oh one (version eight). Questions. Maximum of ninety: multiple choice and performance-based. Time. ninety minutes. Passing score. seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. Launch and old version. V eight launches on or around November seventeen, two thousand twenty-six; V seven (S Y zero seven oh one) retires in two thousand twenty-seven. Price, retake rules. not on the pages this course was built from: confirm on the Comp T I A site. Note. The scale is one hundred to nine hundred, so seven hundred fifty is not seventy-five percent. Do not compute a percentage; aim to understand every objective.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. The figure shows this: The Security plus exam at a glance: ninety questions, ninety minutes, pass at seven hundred fifty of nine hundred, five domains.

1.title: The five domains
1.text: The five domains. one point zero General Security Concepts. Weight: sixteen percent. What it asks: Controls, change management, cryptography. two point zero Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks. Weight: twenty-four percent. What it asks: Actors, vectors, vulnerability types, indicators, A I risks. three point zero Security Architecture. Weight: nineteen percent. What it asks: Architecture models, infrastructure, data protection, resilience. four point zero Security Operations. Weight: twenty-seven percent. What it asks: Hardening, monitoring, identity, automation, incident response. five point zero Security Program Management and Oversight. Weight: fourteen percent. What it asks: Governance, risk, third parties, compliance, audits, awareness. Security Operations is the biggest, followed by Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks. Every domain counts: a weak domain can cost you the pass. Exam tip: V eight expands coverage of A I-related risks, security operations and modern environments. Expect A I threats (prompt injection, poisoning, hallucinations) and A I-assisted automation in questions.

1.title: Question types
1.text: Question types. Multiple choice. What it looks like: A scenario and four or more options; single answer or choose two or three. How to handle it: Read the last sentence first, then the scenario. Performance-based (P B Q). What it looks like: A simulation: match items, drag and drop, order steps, configure a rule, read a log. How to handle it: Skip and return: they take longer; do the quick questions first. P B Qs usually appear early in the exam. Flag them, answer the multiple-choice questions, then come back with the time left. Partial credit may be given on some P B Qs, so never leave one empty.

1.title: How the objectives are worded
1.text: How the objectives are worded. Explain or Describe. Say what it is, why it matters and how it works. Compare and contrast. Tell options apart and choose between them. Given a scenario. Read a situation and pick or apply the right control, step or tool. Summarize. Know the main points and terms. Analyze. Interpret evidence, such as logs or indicators. "Given a scenario" objectives are the practical ones. Learn each concept with a use case and a trade-off.

1.title: A repeatable way to answer
1.text: A repeatable way to answer. Read the last sentence first: what is asked (best, first, most likely, next)? Underline the key facts: the asset, the threat, the constraint (cost, time, legal). Remove options that do not fit the category (a detective control in a "prevent" question). Compare what is left against the key words best, first and most. Mark and move on if you are unsure after a minute. Exam tip: Words that change the answer: B E S T (most appropriate), first (earliest step; often "contain" or "verify"), M O S T likely, L E A S T privilege, not. Read them twice.

1.title: A study plan
1.text: A study plan. one. What to do: Foundations: controls, change, cryptography. Modules: one to three. two. What to do: Threats, vulnerabilities and attacks. Modules: four to eight. three. What to do: Architecture, data and resilience. Modules: nine to eleven. four. What to do: Operations: controls, monitoring, identity, automation, response. Modules: twelve to seventeen. five. What to do: Governance, risk, compliance, audits, awareness. Modules: eighteen to twenty. six. What to do: Final review and practice. Modules: twenty-one. Spaced review: after each module answer its recall questions from memory, then check. Repeat each Quick Reference Card the next day and again after a week. Also learn the acronym list in the objectives: the exam uses many of them.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to know which domain carries the largest weight in Security plus V eight. Which one is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Security Operations. Security Operations is twenty-seven percent, the largest. General Security Concepts is sixteen percent, Architecture nineteen percent and Program Management fourteen percent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate scores seven hundred fifty on the exam. What does that mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The candidate reached the passing score on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred is the passing score. It is not a percentage.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. During the exam a simulation that asks you to drag steps into order looks long. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Flag it, answer the quick questions first and return with the time left. Performance-based questions take longer, so flag them, bank the quick points and return.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A question asks which action should be taken first during an incident. What does the word first tell you? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Choose the earliest appropriate step in the process. first asks for the earliest step in the sequence, such as containing or verifying.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the passing score and scale? Answer: seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. Question two. How many questions and how many minutes? Answer: A maximum of ninety questions in ninety minutes. Question three. Which domain is the largest? Answer: Security Operations (twenty-seven percent).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the two main question types? Answer: Multiple choice and performance-based. Question five. Which part of a question do you read first? Answer: The last sentence. Question six. What does V eight add compared with earlier versions? Answer: More coverage of A I-related risks, security operations and modern environments.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: up to ninety questions (multiple choice and performance-based), ninety minutes, pass at seven hundred fifty of nine hundred. Domains: concepts sixteen percent, threats twenty-four percent, architecture nineteen percent, operations twenty-seven percent, program management fourteen percent. P B Qs: simulations; flag, answer quick questions first, return; never leave empty. Method: last sentence, key facts, remove options, compare with B E S T or first or M O S T, mark and move on. V eight focus: A I risks, security operations, modern environments. In the next module, we continue the course.
